property_summary: After the last play() call resolves, the pot must always be zero if the previous play() call won, or equal to the total tickets bought since the last win otherwise.
After any sequence of calls to play, if the most recent play call resulted in a win (random == 0), then pot must be 0.
After a call to play, the pot must be zero.
After a call to play(), the pot must be zero.
After any play attempt, the contract pot never exceeds the total received tickets plus any initial or final reset, but M refuses to revert and increases by an extra unit beyond what was sent.
The sum of potAfterFirst and potAfterSecond does not exceed the total value sent in the two play calls.
The sum of potAfterFirst and potAfterSecond does not exceed the total value sent in the two play calls.
The sum of potAfterFirst and potAfterSecond does not exceed the total value sent in the two play calls.
The sum of potAfterFirst and potAfterSecond does not exceed the total value sent in the two play calls.
After any play, the pot is non-zero if and only if the last play was a loss.
After any play, the pot is zero if and only if the play was a win.
After any play, the pot can only be zero if the last play was a win or the contract never received a ticket amount.
After a losing play (random != 0), the contract's pot equals the sum of all previously paid ticket amounts.
After any call to play, when the contract's ether balance is non-zero, the public pot must be non-zero.
After a call to play, if the contract's balance is zero then the pot must be zero.
After a successful play where random is 0, the contract's balance is zero or the pot is non-zero, but we exclude cases where the play reverts due to insufficient fee.
After a call to play, if the contract's balance is zero then the pot must be zero.

The sum of the contract balance and the pot variable must equal the total tickets purchased; the bug version breaks this because pot is never incremented, so the invariant fails after a win when pot is reset to 0.

The bank's balance can never exceed FEE_AMOUNT after any sequence of plays, because pot resets to 0 after a win and pot is the sole source of transfers to bank; the bug version violates this as pot is never updated, leaving it permanently 0, so after a win the bank receives FEE_AMOUNT from the contract balance while the contract retains previous play deposits, allowing subsequent wins to transfer more than FEE_AMOUNT to the bank.
After any sequence of play calls, if the last play call did not trigger the win case (no transfer occurred), the pot keeps the total value of all plays.
If the last play() call loses (random != 0), the test contract receives nothing, and the pot is strictly positive after the call.
After calling play, either the test contract's balance increased and the pot is zero, or the balance stayed the same and the pot is positive.
After calling play, either the test contract's balance increased and the pot is zero, or the balance stayed the same and the pot is positive.
After calling play, either the test contract's balance increased and the pot is zero, or the balance stayed the same and the pot is positive.

After any call to play() (win or loss), the pot should equal the sum of all ticket amounts paid minus all payouts; the buggy mutant incorrectly resets pot to 0 on a loss, so after two losses in a row it has pot == 0 instead of 2*TICKET_AMOUNT.

After any number of plays, pot == 0 if the last play was a win; after a loss, pot > 0 and equals the sum of all ticket amounts since the last win. The mutant resets pot to 0 after a loss, breaking the pot > 0 invariant after a single loss.
After a losing play (random != 0), the pot must be greater than zero because no payout occurs; the mutant resets pot to 0 after every play, violating this invariant.

After any number of plays where random == 1 (loss), the pot must equal the sum of ticket amounts paid since the last win; the mutant always resets pot to 0, so after a single loss the pot is 0 instead of accumulating.

After any sequence of calls to play(), pot equals the total msg.value received minus total FEE_AMOUNT sent to bank and minus total payouts to players, modulo the zeroing-on-win; the mutant always zeroes pot even on loss, so after two losses pot becomes 0 instead of 2*TICKET_AMOUNT.
A win never pays out less than the total pot, but M violates this by accepting 1 wei tickets and paying out with the small pot.
After a winning play (random==0), the bank's balance should increase by exactly FEE_AMOUNT; the bug pays the fee to the player instead, leaving the bank's balance unchanged.
